tensions: The favourable lobing zone (1314-1840 Hz) lies entirely ABOVE the ceiling (550 Hz, breakup). Lobing and the ceiling want opposite things here - that is a real tension of this driver combination, not something the filter can resolve.

The breakup divisor is the ramp, not a measurement: at 2.54 this window holds 12 position(s), at the mild endpoint 2.00 it would hold 14. Drive this driver alone with a single tone at the breakup divided by two and measure the SECOND harmonic at the breakup itself; then at the breakup divided by three and measure the THIRD. The lowest harmonic order whose product rises out of the noise floor at the breakup is the divisor: the third silent means 2.0 (only the second reaches the resonance, so a handover an octave below it keeps the resonance out of the passband), the third audible means 3.0. A value in between is only a measurement if BOTH orders were measured and you interpolated between them — then it is your number and the app attributes it to you, never to the ramp it replaces.

uncalibrated: The divisor interpolates between the published endpoints (3 severe, 2 mild); the ramp between them is uncalibrated and needs HD data (spec V6/V9). This ceiling moves if that curve does. To replace it with a measurement: Drive this driver alone at 2844 Hz and measure H2 at 5688 Hz; then at 1896 Hz and measure H3 at the same 5688 Hz. H3 out of the noise floor means the divisor is 3.0, silent means 2.0. A value in between is only a measurement if BOTH orders were measured and you interpolated between them — then it is your number and the app attributes it to you, never to the ramp it replaces.
